text:
ashley: FYI we've got a customer alert — sustained 429s and 500ms+ tail latencies on a dedicated pool in east-1. Throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~40% starting around 09:05 UTC. Opening thread.

derek: Which customer and pool id? Any logs or quick metrics?

ashley: Customer: acme-ux (dedicated pool id dp-948). Spike of tiny requests started ~09:05. Quick metrics snapshot from the period:
```
qps: 1200 -> 2200 (many tiny reqs)
tokens/s: 1.2M -> 720k
GPU util: 35% -> 28%
prefill queue depth: 800 -> 3800
```

maria: That pattern smells like packing/packer failure — lots of tiny requests creating many size=1 microbatches. Any pool config changes recently?

ashley: Current pool config (from console): `max_batch_tokens: "4096"`, `pack_small_requests: "false"`, `quantum_ms: "10"`. No other obvious changes.

ravi: Can you repro locally? Try flooding with many 20–50 token prompts. Example repro script:
```
# repro: flood 2000 clients with tiny prompts
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"x-small","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":20}' &
done
wait
```

derek: Also check packer logs and scheduler traces. Quick command: `kubectl logs packer-0 --since=15m | grep -n "pack failed"` and `kubectl logs scheduler-0 --since=15m | grep quantum`.

maria: From the initial logs I pulled: packer emitted repeated "no compatible slot for tiny request" and the packer loop was draining before enough arrivals could be grouped. Autoscaler looked healthy but didn't scale because `scale_threshold_rps` was 5000 and effective RPS/node stayed under that due to fragmentation.

ashley: I ran ravi's repro locally. Observed lots of single-request microbatches even though request tokens << `max_batch_tokens`. Looks like tenant isolation + `pack_small_requests=false` + low `quantum_ms` means we never wait to batch across arrivals.

ravi: Hypothesis: increase packing window and allow small-request packing. Quick mitigation proposal (canary to 10% nodes):
- enable `pack_small_requests: true`
- increase `quantum_ms` 10 -> 50
- bump `max_batch_tokens` 4096 -> 8192
Also temporarily lower autoscaler threshold from 5000 -> 3000 for dp-948.

derek: +1. Also ensure we have an alert for prefill queue depth so we catch this earlier: `prefill_queue_depth > 2000 for > 2m` -> pager to eng-runtime.

maria: I'll roll a canary to two nodes (node-17,node-18) with that config and run the tiny-request load for 5m to validate. Plan:
1) apply canary config to node-17,node-18
2) run repro script for 5m
3) observe tokens/s, GPU util, single-batch ratio, 429 count

ashley: Canary run results (after config changes):
```
pack_small_requests: true
quantum_ms: 50
max_batch_tokens: 8192
```
Within 2 minutes of canary: tokens/s recovered to ~1.1M, GPU util rose to ~52%, single-request microbatches dropped from 82% -> 9%, 429s returned to baseline.

ravi: Nice. That indicates packing window and allowing cross-tenant small request packing were the main factors. We'll need to document recommended defaults for pools serving high QPS of tiny prompts.

derek: Action items: 
- maria: roll the config to remaining nodes in dp-948 (ETA 30m)
- ravi: write short perf note / internal doc with repro, mitigations, and recommended defaults (quantum_ms >= 50 for tiny-request workloads, pack_small_requests=true, max_batch_tokens tuned to model workloads)
- ashley: follow up with acme-ux with root cause, repro snippet, and mitigation timeline

ashley: Also flagged billing/authging issues earlier — the customer saw repeated 429s which triggered client retries that increased their billing estimate. I'll include that in the customer message and confirm we won't bill for retried failed requests in this window.

infra-bot: Job queued: update-pool dp-948 with `{pack_small_requests: true, quantum_ms: 50, max_batch_tokens: 8192}`. Canary nodes: node-17,node-18.

maria: Canary passed, rolling to rest of dp-948 now. I'll post final metrics in 15m. Thanks all :+1: :tada:

ashley: Leaving this thread open for post-roll observations. If anyone still sees elevated 429s/latency after roll, ping here.
